newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rates rise on short supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rates rise on short supply.

text.p: Croatian money market rates inched up on Monday amid a short supply of kuna funds and poorer liquidity ahead of reserve payments, dealers said.
"Banks' liquidity has worsened generally, causing the supply to shrink today," one dealer told Reuters, adding that some banks were also asking for repayment of previous loans.
By 0900 GMT they withdrew some 20 million kuna and granted 25.4 million in fresh loans, mostly call money.
The call money rate rose to 9.0 from 8.0 percent and the one-week rate inched up to 11 percent from 10.5 earlier.
The banking sector slightly increased its Lombard borrowing to 36 million kuna ahead of today's reserve payments, a central bank official said.

The overall reserve requirement is expected to fall from a fortnight ago after the reserve ratio was cut by two percentage points to 31.85 percent of kuna deposits, which also shrank due to pension payments to around 320 million kuna.
The reserve requirement is now at its lowest in the past 18 months since the central bank started to ease monetary reins.

Seven banks ended last week with some 26 million kuna shortfalls, which they squared in direct trade and overnight money market loans. One bank borrowed 24.7 million kuna for maintaining its reserve position. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
